description: Plan a whole electric-vehicle journey, charge stops included. Give `origin` and `destination` (plus optional `waypoints`) and a `vehicle` — a published profile ("small_hatch", "saloon", "suv", "van") and/or inline figures (battery_kwh, mass_kg, drag_area_m2, aux_kw, connectors) — with `start_soc` (default 0.9), `min_arrival_soc` (default 0.1), `reserve_soc` (default 0.1, the floor the charge must never drop below mid-route), optional `connectors` and `min_kw` filters and `ambient_temperature_c`. Energy comes from a published road-load physics model over the route's own legs; charge times are integrated over the vehicle's charging curve capped by the charge point, NOT energy divided by peak power, which is the single biggest error in naive EV planners. Returns the stops with arrive/depart state of charge, charge time and detour, a per-leg state-of-charge trace, and the journey's driving and charging time. IMPORTANT: when no plan exists — a charger desert, a connector mismatch, a gap wider than the car's range — the answer comes back with `feasible: false`, a `reason` and the furthest point on the route the car can actually reach. That is an ANSWER, not an error to retry: report the reason and never describe it as a plan. `gradient_data` says whether elevation was available: "absent" means consumption was modelled on the flat and under-reads a hilly route. There is no national charge-point registry, so ALWAYS show the returned `coverage_note` — an infeasible plan means "none from these operators", never "there are no chargers here" — and statuses are current only when `availability_live` is true. Requires the MapMap gateway; answers a clear error when the deployment has no charge-point dataset. Display the returned charging_attribution with the plan.

EvVehicleSpec.description:
The vehicle for `plan_ev_route`: one of the published defaults by name,
inline figures, or a named default with inline figures over it.

aux_kw.description:
Auxiliary load in kW — lights, electronics, cabin conditioning.
Winter heating is several times the mild-weather default.

drag_area_m2.description: Drag area (drag coefficient × frontal area), m².

name.description: Display name for the vehicle in the answer.

profile.description:
A published default profile: "small_hatch", "saloon", "suv" or
"van". On its own it selects that vehicle; alongside any inline
figure below it is the base the figure overrides.

usable_fraction.description: Fraction of the gross pack the vehicle will actually use, 0–1.

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

ambient_temperature_c.description:
Ambient temperature in °C. Derates traction energy from a published
study; cabin heating belongs in the vehicle's `aux_kw`.

connectors.description:
Keep only charge points offering at least one of these connector
standards: "type2", "type1", "ccs", "chademo", "tesla", "domestic",
"other". This narrows the vehicle's own set, never widens it.

max_detour_minutes.description:
How far off the route a charge point may sit, as a detour in
minutes (default 15, at most 120).

min_arrival_soc.description: Lowest acceptable state of charge on arrival (default 0.1).

min_kw.description:
Keep only charge points with a usable connector rated at least this
many kW (e.g. 50 for rapid charging only).

reserve_soc.description:
The floor the state of charge must never fall below mid-route
(default 0.1). Distinct from the arrival figure.

start_soc.description: State of charge at the start, 0–1 (default 0.9).

vehicle.description:
The vehicle. Omitted ⇒ the published "saloon" default, and the
answer says which vehicle it used.

waypoints.description:
Intermediate points the route must pass through, in order (at most
8). Charge stops are inserted around them.

name: plan_ev_route

EvPlanLeg.description: One driving leg of the plan, with its state-of-charge bookkeeping.

consumed_wh.description: Battery energy the leg spends, Wh.

end_soc.description: State of charge at the end.

from.description: Where the leg starts: "origin" or a charge point's id.

min_soc.description: Lowest state of charge anywhere within the leg.

regen_wh.description: Battery energy regenerative braking gives back, Wh.

start_soc.description: State of charge at the start of the leg.

to.description: Where it ends: a charge point's id or "destination".

EvPlanSocPoint.description: One point on the state-of-charge trace.

along_route_position.description: How far along the route this point sits, 0.0–1.0.

departing_soc.description: State of charge on leaving, at a charge stop.

soc.description: State of charge on arrival at this point.

EvPlanStop.description: One charge stop in the plan.

along_route_position.description: How far along the route this stop sits, 0.0–1.0.

arrive_soc.description: State of charge on arrival. Never below the reserve floor.

available_now.description:
Whether a bay is free right now. Present only where a live
availability feed backs the claim — absent means unknown, never
"occupied".

charge_s.description:
Time plugged in, seconds — integrated over the vehicle's charging
curve capped by the charge point, not energy ÷ peak power.

charger_kw.description:
That connector's rated power, kW — what the charge time was
computed against.

connector_standard.description: The connector the plan charges on.

dc.description: Whether the connector delivers DC (rapid) rather than AC.

detour_s.description:
Extra driving time this stop costs against going straight past it,
seconds.

name.description: Site name, where the operator publishes one.

off_route_m.description: Straight-line offset from the route geometry, metres.

power_kw_source.description:
"declared" when the operator published the rating, "derived" when it
was computed from voltage × amperage × phases. Never present the two
as the same thing to a user.

source.description: Which operator feed this came from.

status_live.description:
Whether the status came from a live feed rather than the last
ingest.

arrival_soc.description: State of charge on arrival, when the journey is feasible.

energy_kwh.description: Net battery energy the journey costs, kWh.

start_soc.description: State of charge the journey starts at.

stops.description:
How many charge stops the plan contains. Zero on a journey the car
makes on its own — and zero on an infeasible one.

total_distance_m.description: Distance of the planned journey, metres.

total_duration_s.description: Driving plus charging, seconds — the number a user cares about.

availability_live.description:
Whether charge-point statuses came from a live availability feed. A
static planner is the default: without a feed, nothing in this
answer is a claim about which bays are free right now.

charging_attribution.description:
Attribution string for the charge-point operators actually used —
display it with the plan (a licence obligation).

coverage_note.description:
**Always present.** What this deployment's charge-point dataset does
and does not cover. An infeasible plan means "none from these
operators", never "there are no chargers here". Show this alongside
the answer.

feasible.description:
**Whether the journey is possible at all.** False means no plan
exists — a charger desert, a connector mismatch, or a gap wider than
the car's range. Report the `reason` and the furthest reachable
point; never describe an infeasible answer as a plan.

furthest_reachable_lat.description: Latitude of that furthest reachable point.

furthest_reachable_lon.description: Longitude of that furthest reachable point.

furthest_reachable_position.description:
How far along the route the vehicle can get unaided, 0.0–1.0, when
no plan exists.

geometry_polyline6.description:
The planned journey's geometry as an encoded polyline6, through the
charge stops.

gradient_data.description:
"complete", "partial" or "absent". **"absent" means the deployment
had no elevation data and consumption was modelled on the flat**,
which under-reads a hilly route. Say so rather than presenting the
figure as measured.

profile_source.description:
"default" when a published profile supplied the figures, "inline"
when the caller did.

reason.description: The same cause in plain language, for the user.

reason_code.description:
Machine token for why no plan exists, when none does:
"no_chargers_in_corridor", "connector_mismatch", "out_of_range",
"dead_end", "below_min_kw", "chargers_unrated", "stop_limit",
"dataset_empty", "no_charge_curve" or "unroutable".

route_distance_m.description: Distance of the planned route, metres.

route_duration_s.description: Driving time of the planned route, seconds.

soc_trace.description: State of charge at every point of the journey.

stops.description:
The charge stops, in visit order. Always empty when `feasible` is
false: a journey that cannot be completed has no stop list.

vehicle.description: The vehicle the plan was computed for.
